title: Stair Hops
statement: A child climbs a staircase of `n` steps, hopping up either 1 or 2 steps at a time. Return how many different hop sequences reach the top exactly. For example, 3 steps can be climbed as 1+1+1, 1+2, or 2+1.
constraints: The answer fits in a 32-bit integer

keyPoints: The last hop is 1 or 2 steps, so ways(n) = ways(n - 1) + ways(n - 2)
Plain recursion repeats the same calls and takes about 2^n steps
Remember each answer in a map or array so each n is computed once: O(n)
edgeCases: n = 45 (plain recursion is far too slow)
acceptableSlowerApproaches: A loop keeping the last two answers: O(n) time, O(1) space

hints: Think about the last hop. What could it be?
If the last hop is 1 step, the child was on step n - 1; if it is 2, on step n - 2. Add the two counts.
Plain recursion recomputes ways(k) many times. Store each result the first time you compute it.
